attributionsConfirmed: TDD: 'developed by Kent Beck in the late 1990's as part of Extreme Programming' (Fowler bliki, updated 2023-12-11).

Nagappan, Maximilien, Bhat and Williams, Empirical Software Engineering 13:289–302 (2008): 3 Microsoft teams and 1 IBM team; pre-release defect density 40–90 % lower than comparable non-TDD projects (Table 3: 0.61W, 0.38X, 0.24Y, 0.09Z); 15–35 % more development time as management estimates.

Six-month study: Baldassarre et al., 'Studying Test-Driven Development and its Retainment Over a Six-month Time Span', JSS 176 (2021), arXiv 2105.03312: 30 novice developers (third-year students); no effect on external quality or productivity; more tests with higher fault detection.

Fowler, Mocks Aren't Stubs: classical 'use real objects if possible'; mockist 'always use a mock for any object with interesting behavior'; 'Detroit' and 'London' sometimes used; many mockist TDDers dislike that term; outside-in starts by programming the UI using mock layers.
Meszaros vocabulary (dummy, fake, stub, spy, mock) and 'think stunt double' via Fowler's TestDouble and Mocks Aren't Stubs.

SWE at Google ch. 11: small = single process, in many languages a single thread, no sleep, I/O or blocking calls, hermetic in-memory filesystem allowed; medium = multiple processes, localhost; ~80/15/5 by test count; >80 % of GWS pushes rolled back; emergency pushes halved within a year. ch. 12: 'Don't put logic in tests', DAMP.
Google Testing Blog: 70/20/10 first guess (2015); 1.5 % of runs, almost 16 % of tests, 84 % of transitions (2016); 60/75/90 acceptable/commendable/exemplary and no broad top-down mandates (2020).

Goodhart's law: Goodhart 1975 core idea; Strathern 1997 (European Review 5(3):305–321) used the 'When a measure becomes a target...' wording, citing Hoskin (Wikipedia quotation; Cambridge record confirms citation, full text not read).
FIRST: Agile in a Flash post (Ottinger, with Langr): Fast, Isolated, Repeatable, Self-validating, Timely; credited to Brett Schuchert and Tim Ottinger.
QuickCheck: Claessen and Hughes, ICFP '00, Montreal, September 2000, pp. 268–279 (Chalmers research record).

test-flake-diagnosis.rationale: The substitution and logarithm lines were removed and P_clean = (1 − p)^n kept as one reference card whose In words line stands alone; the 37 % and 13 % results stay visible in prose. Recomputed: 0.995^200 = 0.367, 0.995^400 = 0.135 (= 0.367²). Google 2016 figures (1.5 % of runs, almost 16 % of tests, 84 % of pass-to-fail transitions) re-fetched. Smoke-alarm analogy added; its limit (some alarms are real fires; tests can be re-run under controlled order and seeds) is sound. Cart order-dependence and pytest-randomly seed output executed.

questionsRewritten.test-flaky-coverage-mutation-q1: Definition recall replaced by choosing the flaky one among four CI histories; key [2] matches Google's definition (pass and fail on the same code); distractors cover real failures, slow tests and assertion-free tests.
questionsRewritten.test-flaky-coverage-mutation-q4: Arithmetic of 0.995^400 replaced by predicting the effect of doubling the suite (37 % of 37 % ≈ 13 %); formula card removed from the worked example; values recomputed.

test-time-isolation.rationale: Unchanged. Injected-clock boundary test executed; pytest-randomly reseeding and printed seed observed; freezegun/time-machine named only as options (not re-executed). No maths; the flake analogy in the previous lesson covers trust, so no new analogy.

test-line-branch-coverage.rationale: Two percentage formula cards removed; the blended 82 % (7 statements + 2 of 4 branch outcomes = 9/11) is explained in words. coverage.py 7.17.0 re-run on the seven-statement shipping.py: '7 0 4 2 82% 4->7, 7->9'; identical with an assertion-free driver; line-only mode 100 %. q6 rewritten into report interpretation.

questionsRewritten.test-flaky-coverage-mutation-q6: 'Calculate the combined percentage' replaced by interpreting the real report; key [0] and distractors (18 % unrun, 82 % of branches, wrong assertion) checked against the executed report; formula card removed.

Junction/route analogy added. Google 60/75/90 and no-mandate guidance re-fetched. Verifier reworded 'error-handling branch' (React try/catch link).

Planted-typo proofreader analogy added; limit (one mechanical change per run, equivalent mutants as acceptable spellings) sound. Verifier clarified q3's key text.

questionsRewritten.test-flaky-coverage-mutation-q3: Definition recall of 'survived' replaced by triaging a surviving `>` → `>=` retry-limit mutant; verifier reworded the key's ambiguous 'distinguishes 3 attempts from 4' to 'checks what happens when attempts is exactly 3'.

test-mutation-triage.rationale: Lesson unchanged: larger() equivalence re-executed (equal for all small ints; -0.0/0.0 and object identity distinguish it). Google 2018 mutation paper claims unchanged from earlier verification. Verifier fixed a grammatical slip in q10's worked example. No maths; the proofreader analogy in the previous lesson covers equivalent mutants.

questionsRewritten.test-flaky-coverage-mutation-q10: Verifier: worked example 'so the mutant is **equivalent mutant**' corrected to 'so this is an **equivalent mutant**'; content and key unchanged.

test-purpose-boundaries.rationale: Vehicle inspection checklist: a pass covers listed items only, as a green suite covers only checked behaviour; limit (cheap re-runs, regression items, code does not wear out) is accurate. Kept.

test-scope-pyramid.rationale: Bench test / fitted part / test drive maps unit, integration and E2E and why E2E failures localise poorly. Verifier softened the absolute limit about environment-caused failures.

test-shapes-size.rationale: Shapes are shown directly in diagrams and a microservice scenario; the previous lesson's bench/test-drive analogy already covers scope.

test-unit-structure.rationale: Procedural layout guidance (FIRST table, arrange-act-assert, assert syntax) is clearest from the code; a comparison would add length only.

test-pytest-cases.rationale: raises/match, approx and parametrize are API behaviours best learned from executed examples.

test-pytest-fixtures.rationale: Fixture lifetimes are shown precisely by code and the scope table.

test-behaviour-readability.rationale: The brittle-versus-robust test pair is itself the concrete illustration.

test-double-roles.rationale: Film-rehearsal stand-ins map dummy (cut-out), stub (cue reader), spy (note-taker), mock (strict stand-in), fake (understudy) consistently with Meszaros's definitions; limit (one Mock plays several roles; doubles fail silently when they diverge) is accurate.

test-patch-autospec.rationale: Name-binding mechanics are shown exactly by the two-module code and reference diagram; an analogy would blur them.

test-fakes-interactions.rationale: The previous lesson's stand-in analogy covers doubles; the over-mocked test is the concrete illustration here.

test-database-isolation.rationale: Concrete database traces and the SQLite/Postgres contrast carry the ideas.

test-http-browser.rationale: The Orders/Users scenario already makes the seam problem tangible; the contract analogy follows in the next lesson.

test-service-contracts.rationale: Restaurant/supplier checklist maps consumer, contract, provider verification before dispatch and can-i-deploy; verifier corrected the limit from 'response shapes' to the response details the consumer relies on (Pact matching can be exact or type-based).

test-tdd-cycles.rationale: The worked red-green-refactor session is the concrete illustration.

test-properties-shrinking.rationale: Shrinking is shown concretely by the merge counterexample.

test-property-strategies.rationale: Property patterns are taught through a table and runnable examples.

test-flake-diagnosis.rationale: Smoke alarm by the toaster maps flaky test, unrelated triggers and reflexive re-runs, and many sensitive alarms to suite-level compounding; limit (some alarms are real fires; tests can be reproduced under controlled order and seeds) is accurate.

test-time-isolation.rationale: Clock injection is shown directly in code; the previous lesson's analogy covers trust.

test-line-branch-coverage.rationale: The real coverage report is the concrete object; the next lesson's route analogy covers branch versus path.

test-path-coverage-limits.rationale: Every turn versus every route maps branch outcomes and execution paths, and places the cost = 10 bug on one route; limit (infeasible and unbounded routes; coverage does not check results) is accurate.

test-mutant-boundaries.rationale: Planted typos for a proofreader map mutants, killed and surviving, with equivalent mutants as acceptable spellings; limit (one mechanical change per run, cost) is accurate.

test-mutation-triage.rationale: The previous lesson's proofreader analogy already covers equivalent mutants; the larger() code is concrete.
